# OMP Strata

Current qualification (2026-10-28): stock Strata v0.2.7 (engine 0.1.52) + stock OMP 18.13.2 on the PRO,
RTX 5090 131K default, pair stock-roles profile and Studio route. Current candidate:
`win11-rtxpro6000-iq3s-262k-slots4-parking-strata0.2.7-omp18.13.2`.
The pair's automatic conversation cache is off after the engine locked its 26.8 GiB PLE table in RAM; G19 follows
that reported state. These selections roll back to v0.2.3. The RTX 5090 262K opt-in stays on qualified v0.2.3
with its v0.2.1 rollback; its v0.2.7 draft is held on RAM headroom. The unmeasured pair default-split draft stays
unqualified. Current selections and evidence: https://github.com/alphastorm/omp-strata/blob/main/docs/DECISION.md.

> Profile, lifecycle tool and acceptance evidence for running the stock Oh My Pi (OMP) coding agent against
> a stock, local Strata inference server on one Windows 11 + RTX host. It forks neither project and adds no
> proxy: every download is pinned by URL, size and SHA-256; stock `setup.py` runs unmodified from verified
> local inputs; Strata binds to loopback behind an API key; stock OMP runs in an isolated profile with every
> model role on the local server and no cloud fallback. Python standard library only. Earlier qualification (2026-10-23): stock
> Strata v0.2.3 (engine 0.1.48) + stock OMP 18.12.6 on the RTX 4090 + RTX 3090 pair in `rtx3090-win-a` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
> IQ3_S at the trained 262,144-token context, stock layer split with stock roles `--gpu-roles 0=main,1=helper` putting the
> RTX 4090 as Main staged last, pipeline windows 2 and the engine's 8 GiB conversation cache,
> no batch slots, display on the RTX 4090; `win11-rtx3090-rtx4090-iq3s-262k-pw2-disp4090-roles-parking-strata0.2.3-omp18.12.6`;
> [ledger](https://github.com/alphastorm/omp-strata/blob/main/releases/win11-rtx3090-rtx4090-iq3s-262k-pw2-disp4090-roles-parking-strata0.2.3-omp18.12.6/qualification.json)),
> on an RTX PRO 6000 at the trained 262,144-token context with four batch slots, the engine's 8 GiB conversation parking and 32K chunks
> (`win11-rtxpro6000-iq3s-262k-slots4-parking-strata0.2.3-omp18.12.6`;
> [ledger](https://github.com/alphastorm/omp-strata/blob/main/releases/win11-rtxpro6000-iq3s-262k-slots4-parking-strata0.2.3-omp18.12.6/qualification.json)),
> and on an RTX 5090 at 131,072 tokens (`win11-rtx5090-coder-iq1m-131k-strata0.2.3-omp18.12.6`;
> [ledger](https://github.com/alphastorm/omp-strata/blob/main/releases/win11-rtx5090-coder-iq1m-131k-strata0.2.3-omp18.12.6/qualification.json)).
> Qualified opt-in by the owner on 2026-10-23: RTX 5090 Coder IQ1_M at 262,144 tokens
> (`win11-rtx5090-coder-iq1m-262k-strata0.2.3-omp18.12.6`;
> [ledger](https://github.com/alphastorm/omp-strata/blob/main/releases/win11-rtx5090-coder-iq1m-262k-strata0.2.3-omp18.12.6/qualification.json)),
> with a 36 GiB available-RAM startup floor, 21 pass and 3 not applicable. The 131K profile remains the RTX 5090's
> current/default; this is an explicit opt-in.
> Stock Strata v0.1.40.3 + stock OMP 18.8.4 stays qualified for single-card RTX 3090 hosts
> ([ledger](https://github.com/alphastorm/omp-strata/blob/main/releases/win11-rtx3090-coder-iq1m-131k-strata0.1.40.3-omp18.8.4/qualification.json)).
> Each host rolls back to v0.2.1 (engine 0.1.46) + OMP 18.10.1:
> [PRO, 262K](https://github.com/alphastorm/omp-strata/blob/main/releases/win11-rtxpro6000-iq3s-262k-slots4-parking-strata0.2.1-omp18.10.1/qualification.json),
> [RTX 5090, 131K](https://github.com/alphastorm/omp-strata/blob/main/releases/win11-rtx5090-coder-iq1m-131k-strata0.2.1-omp18.10.1/qualification.json),
> [RTX 5090, 262K opt-in](https://github.com/alphastorm/omp-strata/blob/main/releases/win11-rtx5090-coder-iq1m-262k-strata0.2.1-omp18.10.1/qualification.json),
> [pair, 262K default split](https://github.com/alphastorm/omp-strata/blob/main/releases/win11-rtx3090-rtx4090-iq3s-262k-pw2-disp4090-parking-strata0.2.1-omp18.10.1/qualification.json);
> the default and split-32 v0.2.3 pair drafts and the v0.1.44.1 pair release remain draft, not qualified.
> Each current ledger has 21 pass and 3 not applicable. Real-host receipts cite `5726674` on the PRO, RTX 5090 131K and
> RTX 5090 262K main runs, with reruns at `a915c69` (PRO G10, 131K G20, 262K G19), and `a915c69` on the pair roles main
> run with its G18 rerun at `de60693` (operator receipts G01-G05 cite `a915c69`; host-free G06 cites `5726674`).
> Retained main-run failures stay beside their passing reruns: PRO G10 (deep artifact rehash counted one problem while
> the server ran, not reproduced), 131K G20 (compared scheduled task run states), 262K G19 (expected parking the engine
> left off), and pair G18 (fact lost after compaction). Engine 0.1.48 sizes its own conversation cache from free RAM
> after load (Strata#3493: 8,192 MiB on the PRO and pair, 1,024-1,280 MiB on the RTX 5090 131K, off on the RTX 5090
> 262K), so profiles drop the pinned `--conversation-cache-mib 8192` tip while G19 follows `/metrics`; PRO and pair
> disk floors rise from 90 to 91 GiB for the MTP drafter fetch while 5090 disk floors stay 90 and RAM floors stay
> unchanged. Scored (G24): PRO 17/18 (pilot 5/6; v0.2.1: 17/18), RTX 5090 131K 17/18 (pilot 6/6; v0.2.1: 17/18),
> 262K opt-in 14/18 (pilot 6/6; v0.2.1: 15/18), pair roles 14/18 (pilot 5/6; v0.2.1 pair: 16/18). Per task: tool-loop
> 2/3 on PRO and RTX 5090 131K, and 0/3 on RTX 5090 262K opt-in and pair; multifile-regression 2/3 on 262K opt-in;
> bugfix-b 2/3 on pair; every other task 3/3. Malformed-arguments counters are 0 across all four v0.2.3 profiles (one
> `tool_call_cap` abort with `calls_without_results: 1` each on the 262K opt-in and the pair); all task failures stay
> counted. Scored batch walls are 578 s on the PRO (v0.2.1: 623 s), 847 s on the RTX 5090 131K (771 s), 831 s on the
> 262K opt-in (778 s) and 1,183 s on the pair (v0.2.1: 1,051 s); these are not isolated decode latency. v0.2.3 ships
> its engine (0.1.48) as a separately versioned CUDA 13 component tarball staged into `runtime\strata\engine\`, with
> `locks/strata-python-cp313-win_amd64-strata0.2.3.txt` (certifi 2026.10.19 + truststore 0.10.5); OMP 18.10.2+ task
> subagents answer in plain text and `--restore` (18.10.3) is admitted like `--resume`.
> Owner decision on 2026-10-23: on `rtx3090-win-a`, engine 0.1.48's stage order was admitted after the pair measurement
> (#48), where stock roles (`--gpu-roles 0=main,1=helper`, RTX 4090 as Main staged last; layers 0-23 / 24-47) read a
> 100K-token prompt in 31.2 s against 36.2 s for the default (K=25) and 29.1 s for manual split 32 (prompt reading at
> 100K: 3,300 vs 2,839 vs 3,534 tok/s; decode 144-174 tok/s for roles; v0.1.43.1 on 2026-10-21 with driver 617.42:
> 28.6 s); the owner selected the roles variant as current, with v0.2.1 as rollback. The PRO and RTX 5090 v0.1.44.1
> (including 262K opt-in), v0.1.43.1 and v0.1.43 profiles, the pair's v0.1.43.1 and v0.1.43 profiles, and each host's
> v0.1.42 + OMP 18.8.9 profiles stay earlier qualified history. All earlier failed gates and passing reruns remain
> published.
> The pair's [earlier qualified 131K profile](https://github.com/alphastorm/omp-strata/blob/main/releases/win11-rtx3090-rtx4090-iq3s-131k-pw2-disp4090-strata0.1.42-omp18.8.9/qualification.json)
> keeps the display on the RTX 4090; its
> [earlier predecessor](https://github.com/alphastorm/omp-strata/blob/main/releases/win11-rtx3090-rtx4090-iq3s-131k-pw2-strata0.1.42-omp18.8.9/qualification.json)
> requires moving the display back to the RTX 3090. Single-card RTX 3090 profiles are not rollbacks
> while both cards are installed: they name GPU 0, now the RTX 4090. Earlier qualified history: on the RTX PRO 6000, stock Strata v0.1.41 + stock OMP
> 18.8.6 with the same choices at 262,144 tokens, then at 131,072 tokens, then the same choices on v0.1.40.3 + OMP
> 18.8.4, then OMP 18.8.3, then v0.1.40.2 + 18.8.0 without them; on the RTX 5090, v0.1.41 + OMP 18.8.6, then
> v0.1.40.3 + OMP 18.8.4, then stock Strata v0.1.34 + stock OMP 18.4.10, which also stays qualified on the
> single-card RTX 3090 and RTX 4090. Community project; not affiliated with or endorsed by the
> Oh My Pi maintainers, the Strata maintainer, Qwen or NVIDIA.

## Install

- From a checkout, with the current candidate profile: `validate` → `fetch` → `install` → `keygen` →
  `start` → `launch-omp` → `stop` (`py -3 scripts\omp_strata.py <command> --profile <profile> --root <root>`).
- One integration root per candidate; nothing is written to the user's normal OMP configuration or to
  `%APPDATA%\Strata`.

## Boundaries

- Supported: the qualified profiles under `profiles/` (Windows 11, a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000, RTX 5090, RTX 3090
  or RTX 4090, or the RTX 4090 + RTX 3090 layer-split pair; every other profile is a draft or a rollback installation),
  text only, single user, loopback only.
- Remote use: the Mac Studio's current qualified route, `client-rtxpro6000-262k-strata0.2.3-omp18.12.6`, runs stock
  OMP 18.12.6 through an SSH local forward to `win11-rtxpro6000-iq3s-262k-slots4-parking-strata0.2.3-omp18.12.6`,
  the PRO's current v0.2.3 262K profile. Its independent G23 passed on 2026-10-23 at `de60693`: missing key refused
  before launch, wrong key 401, health RTT 4.6-5.2 ms and stream TTFT 0.171 s; tunnel drop failed the turn in flight
  with the prior transcript preserved, and nonce recall passed after tunnel reopen (0.77 s), client restart (0.71 s)
  and verified server restart (2.67 s). Its qualified rollback, `client-rtxpro6000-262k-strata0.2.1-omp18.10.1`,
  reaches the PRO's v0.2.1 262K rollback. The 0.1.44.1, 0.1.43.1, 0.1.43 and 0.1.42 262K routes and
  `client-rtxpro6000-strata0.1.41-omp18.8.6` 131K route stay earlier history.
- Not supported: images, remote clients other than those qualified current and rollback Mac-to-RTX PRO 6000 routes, other
  operating systems, durable engine state across restarts, multiple tenants. Comparisons with other runtimes are
  separate, comparison-only tools.
- Security: loopback only, API key required on every model, control and metrics route, key in a user-only
  file, ambient provider credentials scrubbed from OMP's environment, no telemetry. Not a sandbox, a
  multi-tenant service or an egress firewall.
